highlights: Graph v2 on held-out issues: the hybrid ranks the file to fix first in 54.3% of issues (+4.7), BM25 in 43.7% (+6.1); with dense alone the gain (+1.5) is not significant.

Weights tuned on all of Lite chose no graph hop: the gain comes from symbols and paths the issue names, weighted by mention (traceback and path 3, Class.method 2, in code 1, bare word 0.3, rarer names count more), at most 15 seed files.

B5b: a strong model with grep already finds the file in about 90% of Lite issues; it used a graph tool in 123 of 300 and walked the graph (get_neighbour, impact) in 56; graph tools were 9.7% of its calls.
Held-out Verified issues include 71 multi-file fixes, so Recall@k and Acc@k differ there; on Lite every fix is one file.
Not comparable: LLM localizers (Agentless about 73% Acc@1, LocAgent about 78% with Claude 3.5 Sonnet) against B5a; they are comparable to B5b, though llm_1 is a newer model.
Cost: B5a and retry about 140M embedding tokens (about $2.80); B5b about 57M prompt tokens across both arms, 77% cached.

B5c no LLM: the graph signal reorders the top 5 files on 323 of 500 tasks; file coverage 29.4 → 31.6 and precision 20.5 → 22.1 (micro, p < 0.001), weights as chosen on SWE-bench Lite, not tuned on ContextBench. The gain is mostly Python (41.9 → 46.5); TypeScript, JavaScript and Go are flat.

B5c agent: graph tools ahead on all 8 measures (file to line, coverage and precision) by 0.4–1.6 points, none significant; largest on fixes spanning 2–3 files (+2.9 file coverage, +3.3 line coverage, p 0.04, one of about 30 slices tested).

B5c against ContextBench's published tables (macro): our agent's file F1 0.579 is the best listed; coverage is second to Prometheus; symbol and span F1 sit behind GPT-5 and Devstral 2. Not like for like: our agent is asked for the context directly, and uses a newer model.
method: B5a: SWE-bench Lite file localization without an LLM. Each of the 300 test issues' repo, at its base commit, goes through PipesHub's code-graph pipeline in memory; files are ranked by BM25 (SWE-bench's own baseline), dense retrieval with embedding_1 over PipesHub's own embedding units, and their hybrid, each with and without a code-graph signal. Fusion weights are chosen on the 23 dev issues, then frozen. B5b: llm_1 (gpt-5.6-luna on Azure) localizes the same 300 issues in two arms with the same prompt and a 30-turn limit: search only (regex grep over the whole repo, file reads, directory listing) and the same plus PipesHub's full Code Graph toolset as its agents see it, over that commit's graph. Both submit up to 10 ranked files. Test files are candidates for no B5a method. ContextBench is deferred to B4/B6.
question: How does PipesHub do on benchmarks people already know?
repos: SWE-bench Lite: 300 test issues from 12 Python repos (django 114, sympy 77, matplotlib 23, scikit-learn 23, pytest 17, sphinx 16, astropy, requests, pylint, xarray, seaborn, flask); 23 dev issues from 6 other repos for tuning.
summary: B5a (no LLM): PipesHub's dense retrieval beats SWE-bench's BM25 baseline by 7.7 points at Acc@1 on Lite. The first graph signal lowered top-1; a retry that weights symbols by how the issue mentions them, tuned on Lite and scored once on 407 held-out SWE-bench Verified issues, raises the hybrid's Acc@1 from 49.6 to 54.3 (p = 0.004) and BM25's from 37.6 to 43.7 (p = 0.003). B5b (agent, llm_1): with grep and file reads the agent localizes 89.7% of Lite issues at Acc@1; adding PipesHub's code-graph tools gives 90.3%, inside noise (p 0.80), at 44% more prompt tokens and 51% more time. B5c (ContextBench, 500 tasks in 8 languages, official scorer): without an LLM, the same graph signal with B5a's weights raises BM25's file coverage from 29.4% to 31.6% (p < 0.001), a third held-out confirmation; with an agent, PipesHub's graph tools add 0.4–1.6 points on every measure (not significant) at 33% more prompt tokens.
